primary_text_note: Meera Syal, Anita and Me (1996) is in copyright. Quotations verified against LitCharts, GradeSaver and the published fete passage; page numbers as cited by those guides.

findings.claim: Sam Lowbridge “declares ‘We are the British’” at the village fete (L4 content, key fact, conclusion, exam tip, KC options, flashcard; L6 content + flashcard; L7 content, memorisation list, KC match; L5 KC options).
findings.truth: Sam has no such line. At the Spring Fete he heckles: “Yow don't do nothing but talk, ‘Uncle’. And give everything away to some darkies we've never met. We don't give a toss for anybody else. This is our patch. Not some wogs' handout.” The lessons now quote the clean fragment “This is our patch”; the slur is deliberately not printed on a student page.
findings.evidence: GradeSaver ch.7 summary + superprof quotation of the fete passage; LitCharts Sam Lowbridge character page (fete outburst, age 16).

findings.claim: “I'm not lying, I'm just telling a story” given as Meena's line (L1, L2, L6, L7 + 4 flashcards + 1 knowledge check + 1 KC distractor).
findings.truth: Fabricated. The real p.10 line is “I'm not really a liar, I just learned very early on that those of us deprived of history sometimes need to turn to mythology to feel complete, to belong.” Edits quote from “I just learned very early on...”, the stretch both sources agree on.
findings.evidence: LitCharts quotes page (litcharts.com/lit/anita-and-me/quotes) p.10; GradeSaver quotes + chapter summaries (gradesaver.com/anita-and-me) p.10.

findings.claim: “I wanted to be them. I wanted their life.” given as Meena's line (L2, L3, L6, L7 + 3 flashcards + 1 knowledge check + KC match).
findings.truth: Fabricated; no reliable source carries it. Replaced with the verified p.149-150 line: “I knew I was a freak of some kind, too mouthy, clumsy and scabby to be a real Indian girl, too Indian to be a real Tollington wench...”

findings.claim: “If you can't fit in, you might as well stand out” given as Meena's closing line (L5 content + exam tip, L6 content, L7 content + 4 flashcards + KC options).
findings.truth: Fabricated. Replaced with the verified end of the same p.149-150 sentence, “living in the grey area between all categories felt increasingly like home”, and with p.303 for the ending.
findings.evidence: LitCharts quotes page (litcharts.com/lit/anita-and-me/quotes) p.149-150 and p.303.

findings.claim: “This is also my home” given as a family/Meena quotation (L4, L5 content + flashcard, L7 memorisation list + KC match).
findings.truth: Fabricated. The real claim of belonging is p.303: “The place in which I belonged was wherever I stood and there was nothing stopping me simply moving forward and claiming each resting place as home.”

findings.claim: “I did not have a name for what I felt” given as Meena's identity-crisis line (L4 content + flashcard + KC distractor, L7 memorisation list + flashcard).
findings.truth: Fabricated. Replaced with verified lines (“I knew I was a freak of some kind” / “too Indian to be a real Tollington wench”).

findings.claim: “Papa works at a factory despite being overqualified… professional qualifications from India were often not recognised in Britain” (L2 content + flashcard, L6 content + KC + 2 flashcards, L7 content + flashcard).
findings.truth: Papa has an office job. The novel refers to “the office” and “his day at the office, which he never talks about”; he is promoted mid-novel and the family gain a bigger home. The tyre factory belongs to Roberto Rutter. Nothing in the text says his Indian qualifications were refused.
findings.evidence: LitCharts Mr. Kumar (Papa) character page (office, promotion, “whatever he did to make money was not what papa really was”); LitCharts characters page (Roberto Rutter works at a tyre factory). Same fault was found in the AQA unit for this novel.

findings.claim: “Anita's father is absent” (L3), “her absent father” (L6), “the absent father” (L7).
findings.truth: Reversed. Roberto (Mr Rutter) stays with the girls and works at a tyre factory; it is Deirdre who runs off, seen kissing and leaving with Dave ‘the Poet’ at the Diwali fair.
findings.evidence: LitCharts characters page (Roberto Rutter) and plot summary (“Deirdre abandons the family”).

findings.claim: “She steals sweets from Mr Ormerod's shop” (L2 content, L5 content) and the knowledge check “What does Meena steal from Mr Ormerod's shop?” keyed to “Sweets”.
findings.truth: Meena steals the charity collection tin from the shop counter and lets Baby take the blame; Anita is the one who steals sweets. The key marked the true answer wrong.
findings.evidence: GradeSaver quotes + chapter summaries (gradesaver.com/anita-and-me) ch.6 summary; LitCharts plot summary (“participates in stealing money from a charity drive, falsely blaming other children”).

findings.claim: “The novel ends with Meena winning a scholarship to a prestigious school and leaving Tollington” (L5 content, conclusion, KC, flashcard; L6 content).
findings.truth: Meena passes the eleven-plus and wins a grammar school place; it is the whole family, not Meena alone, that moves out of Tollington. No scholarship is awarded.
findings.evidence: GradeSaver quotes + chapter summaries (gradesaver.com/anita-and-me) plot summary (“Meena passes her exam, the family leaves Tollington”); LitCharts plot summary.

findings.claim: Nanima arrives “during Meena's illness” (L4 content, L6 content + key fact + flashcard).
findings.truth: Order reversed. Nanima comes from India to help with the newborn Sunil, well before the riding accident; she returns to India while Meena is still in hospital.
findings.evidence: GradeSaver quotes + chapter summaries (gradesaver.com/anita-and-me) plot summary; LitCharts plot summary.

findings.claim: The turning point is repeatedly called “Meena's illness” (L4 heading, description, key fact, conclusion, exam tip, KC options, match pairs, practice question, flashcard; L5 and L6 content).
findings.truth: Meena is never ill. At the stables she learns Anita is going out with Sam, tries to ride away, is thrown from the horse and severely injures her leg, which puts her in hospital for a long stay.
findings.evidence: GradeSaver quotes + chapter summaries (gradesaver.com/anita-and-me) plot summary (“attempts to flee on horseback but is thrown and severely injures her leg, leaving her hospitalized”).

findings.claim: “For Edexcel Component 1 Section B…” (L1 exam tip) and “Which assessment objectives are tested in Edexcel Component 1 Section B?” (L7 knowledge check).
findings.truth: Banned house strings (“Component 1”, “Section B”). Reworded to “the post-1914 novel essay”. The AO answer itself (AO1, AO3, AO4) is correct and is unchanged.

findings.claim: “For AO2, discuss how Syal uses the structure of the novel…” (L4 exam tip) and “For AO2, analyse the structural arc of the Bildungsroman…” (L5 exam tip).
findings.truth: AO2 is not assessed on the post-1914 novel essay. That section carries AO1 16 + AO3 16 + AO4 8 = 40. Telling students to write for AO2 sends them after marks that do not exist. The advice is kept but the AO label is dropped.
findings.evidence: specs/edexcel/english-literature-1ET0.md lines 1115-1130 (“Assessment Objectives covered are AO1, AO3 and AO4”) and the raw-mark table at 1312-1400.

findings.claim: “Windrush generation: the generation of people who emigrated from Caribbean and South Asian countries to Britain between 1948 and 1971” (L1 glossary + in-text definition + flashcard).
findings.truth: The Windrush generation is Caribbean migration. South Asian migration was a separate, later wave — which is what the Kumars belong to. As written, a student could label Meena's family Windrush in an AO3 paragraph.
findings.evidence: L1's own body text already says “The Windrush generation arrived from the Caribbean in 1948, and significant South Asian immigration followed”.

findings.claim: All 42 practice questions are labelled “40 marks — Post-1914 Essay”, but 35 of them carry a 20-mark band ladder (“Top band (17-20)… Upper band (13-16)… Top band (9-12)” — note “Top band” twice and “Upper band”, neither in the house ladder). Only the seven ‘how far do you agree’ questions use the correct 25–32 + 8 scale. Nine of the mark-scheme strings also quote the fabricated lines (F1–F6), and several still say “illness” or “scholarship”.
findings.truth: The post-1914 essay is 40 marks: 32 for AO1 + AO3 with 8 for AO4. Every ladder should run to 32 + 8, using the house band names (Top / Upper-mid / Mid / Lower-mid / Low / Basic). Two options: (a) regenerate all 42 ‘marks’ strings in one pass on the 32 + 8 ladder with the corrected quotations — recommended, since the 178-ladder relabel queue already exists and a surgical swap here would be overwritten by it; or (b) hand-patch only the nine quote-bearing strings now and leave the ladder wrong. RULING (coordinator, 2 Sep): ladder rescale stays in the corpus queue; the nine quote-bearing marks strings are patched here, quotation only, ladder untouched. Residual for the queue: band scale on 35 questions, plus prose slips ('stealing sweets', 'illness', 'scholarship') inside marks strings.
findings.evidence: spec raw-mark table lines 1312-1400 (Questions 7 to 30: AO1 16, AO3 16, AO4 8 = 40); CHECK_PROMPT house ladder.

findings.claim: “The moment Meena finally rejects Anita is one of the novel's most significant scenes… Meena walks away.”
findings.truth: There is no such scene. The friendship ends across three events: Meena overhearing Anita boast about the ‘Paki-bashing’ with Sam, the riding accident and hospital stay, and the night Tracey falls in the pond — after which Meena tells the truth and never hears from Anita again. Reworded as a break that builds, not a single walk-away.
findings.evidence: GradeSaver quotes + chapter summaries (gradesaver.com/anita-and-me) plot summary; LitCharts plot summary.

findings.claim: “Practise writing under timed conditions (55 minutes for one essay).”
findings.truth: Not wrong, but tight against the clock: the paper is 1h45 for two sections of 40 marks each, so 55 minutes here leaves 50 for the Shakespeare two-part question. Defensible teaching advice; left alone.

summary: Every lesson carries at least one mark-affecting error. All six ‘key quotations to memorise’ are fabricated, and the two biggest plot facts are wrong the same way the AQA unit was: Papa works in an office (the tyre factory is Roberto Rutter's) and it is Deirdre, not Anita's father, who leaves. Also fixed: the theft (charity tin, not sweets) and its wrongly keyed knowledge check, the ‘illness’ that is really a broken leg, Nanima's arrival order, the ending (eleven-plus and grammar school, whole family moves), two AO2 instructions on a section where AO2 is not assessed, and two banned spec-code strings. One item left to adjudicate: all 42 practice mark schemes run on a 20-mark ladder under a 40-mark label.
